fixes.explanation: Yep, a boat. The crowds got so large that Jesus got into a boat and sat down, while all the people stood on the shore (Matthew 13:2). I think that's a pretty smart spot to teach from. Crowd on the shore, Jesus in the boat.

A rooftop would be a fun spot, but the text doesn't put Him there. Jesus had just gone out of the house and sat by the sea (Matthew 13:1). When the crowds got large, He got into a boat and sat down. The people stood on the shore (Matthew 13:2).

Goats would make a fun story, but Jesus never mentions one. He says some seed fell along the path, and the birds came and devoured it (Matthew 13:4). A goat wandering in would be a whole different parable. The answer is birds.

True. Jesus says that when the sun rose, the seedlings were scorched (Matthew 13:6). That seed had sprung up quickly because the soil was shallow (Matthew 13:5). Then the sun rose and it did not go well.

No root, that's the problem. Jesus says the seedlings were scorched, and they withered because they had no root (Matthew 13:6). I've seen cookies that looked great on the tray and fell apart when I picked them up, so I get it. Something was missing underneath.

That would be a sad harvest, and that's not the story. The seed on good soil produced a crop, a hundredfold, sixtyfold, or thirtyfold (Matthew 13:8). That's much more than what went in, not less. After the path, the rocky ground and the thorns, this ending turns things around.

True. Jesus says, “The knowledge of the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven has been given to you, but not to them.” (Matthew 13:11). He is talking to the disciples there. The word “given” tells me this knowledge came as a gift to them.

Doubling isn't the word Jesus uses. He says whoever has will be given more, and he will have an abundance (Matthew 13:12). For whoever does not have, “…even what he has will be taken away from him.” (Matthew 13:12). So the answer is taken away.

That's it. Jesus says, “Though seeing, they do not see; though hearing, they do not hear or understand.” (Matthew 13:13). He then quotes Isaiah, who says they hardly hear with their ears, and they have closed their eyes (Matthew 13:15). So the reason is that they do not see or understand.
Jesus doesn't say that. He says, “But blessed are your eyes because they see, and your ears because they hear.” (Matthew 13:16). He says they see and they hear. Nothing in the line points to later.

The evil one. Jesus says, “…the evil one comes and snatches away what was sown in his heart. This is the seed sown along the path.” (Matthew 13:19). It's about someone who hears the message of the kingdom but does not understand it. What was sown in his heart gets snatched away.

False prophets aren't mentioned in this passage. Jesus names the evil one, who comes and snatches away what was sown in his heart (Matthew 13:19). That's the one doing the snatching. Nobody else in His explanation of the path takes the seed.

Fighting back isn't in the picture here. Jesus says that when trouble or persecution comes because of the word, he quickly falls away (Matthew 13:21). This is the one who has no root and remains for only a season. Joy at the start, then gone when trouble shows up.

Unfruitful. Jesus says the worries of this life and the deceitfulness of wealth choke the word, “…and it becomes unfruitful.” (Matthew 13:22). Remember the thorns that grew up and choked the seedlings (Matthew 13:7)? Same picture, only now it's worries and the deceitfulness of wealth doing the crowding.

He understands it. Jesus says, “But the seed sown on good soil is the one who hears the word and understands it.” (Matthew 13:23). Back on the path, the one who heard did not understand it (Matthew 13:19). This one hears, understands, and bears fruit.
